teams.heading: Fiji's Saturday opponents Ireland lose captain Dan Sheehan to concussion
teams.body: The IRFU confirmed on Monday that hooker Dan Sheehan will miss Saturday's match at the Aviva Stadium. The 28-year-old was forced off for a head injury assessment just before half-time in Friday's 42-12 win over Argentina and is in a 12-day return-to-play protocol. Gus McCarthy has been called in to train with the squad, and Sheehan, who was captain in the absence of the injured Caelan Doris, is a doubt for the South Africa game.

lead.why: It is the freshest new development in the pack and changes the make-up of Fiji's Saturday opponents, though it is an Ireland item and the lead is a judgement call.

teams.heading: Jack van Poortvliet says England played with 'extra edge' for Steve Borthwick
teams.body: Jack van Poortvliet has admitted that the week's criticism of Steve Borthwick in the broadsheets found its way into England's performance against Australia. The scrum-half said the playing group and staff had held a conversation about it and backed the head coach, adding: "there was an extra edge to do well for Steve". He also looked back on a difficult first half, when a Max Jorgensen intercept led to a try, before a Tommy Freeman pass sent him clear for his own score straight after the break.

lead.why: It is a fresh, first-hand player response that ties the week's criticism of Borthwick to England's performance, and it avoids repeating the already-reported result.

teams.heading: Erasmus tips Kalvin Gourgues to start at flyhalf for France
teams.body: Fabien Galthié is short of flyhalves after Romain Ntamack injured his shoulder against Fiji, and South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus reckons the France coach will pick a more physical 10 this week. He anticipates 21-year-old centre Kalvin Gourgues starting at flyhalf, with scrum-half Maxime Lucu, who has played 10 for Bordeaux Bègles and France, coming off the bench once the game opens up. Dupont, who is set to lead Les Bleus, adds a wildcard, because Erasmus admits he is not sure his teammates always know what the skipper will do next.

lead.why: It is the France selection question of the day, with France short at flyhalf and the Boks' coach predicting the answer.

teams.heading: Dan Sheehan out of Fiji game; Sean Jansen ruled out of championship
teams.body: Dan Sheehan will miss Saturday's Nations Championship game against Fiji after a concussion suffered against Argentina, with the IRFU confirming a 12-day return-to-play protocol. The captain was forced off for a head injury assessment just before half-time on Friday and never returned. Sean Jansen is out of the rest of the championship with a knee injury, and returns to Connacht for rehabilitation. Leinster's Gus McCarthy and Ulster's David McCann have been called in to train with the squad this week.

lead.why: It is a new, material change to Ireland's squad: the captain is out of the Fiji game and a second forward is out of the championship.

teams.heading: Marco Riccioni returns to Italy squad for Argentina test in Genoa
teams.body: Marco Riccioni is available again for Saturday's Argentina test in Genoa, the Perpignan prop with 39 caps rejoining the squad. The group stays in Turin before travelling to Genoa on Thursday. Niccolò Cannone, the Benetton second-row, said after the Springboks defeat that Italy must bring everything that failed in Turin and take a step forward in every area.

teams.heading: Australia's 45-22 Twickenham defeat leaves Scotland facing a fairer fight
teams.body: England beat Australia 45-22 at Twickenham, and Planet Rugby's post-match column suggests Scotland's next opponents are more vulnerable than the scoreline alone implies. The writer describes a team with a "revolving cast" at fly-half, porous defence and an inability to control possession. Captain Harry Wilson said England "put us under the pump, we didn't get too much ball in the first half." The column argues the pressure will eventually fall on new coach Les Kiss, whose squad has too many players short of Test standard.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the pack that bears on Scotland's next opponent, and it rests on a concrete result, England's 45-22 win over Australia.

teams.heading: Tom Shanklin wants Dan Edwards to replace Sam Costelow at 10
teams.body: Sam Costelow started the 28-21 win over Japan, with Dan Edwards coming off the bench in the second half, and former Wales centre Tom Shanklin says Edwards should start against New Zealand. "I'd go with Dan Edwards at 10," said Shanklin, who wants more ball movement from the fly-half against the All Blacks. Former scrum-half Richie Rees and ex-wing Shane Williams disagree, urging head coach Steve Tandy to keep Costelow for continuity, with Williams warning a switch could strip Costelow of confidence.

lead.why: It is a new item from the BBC on Wales's selection at 10 ahead of the All Blacks, the most debated team question in the pack.

teams.heading: Contepomi adds two hookers and Medrano to Pumas squad for Genoa
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi has been forced to shuffle his group before Saturday's test in Genoa. Matías Medrano, uncapped and at Benetton this season, replaces Rodrigo Martínez, while hookers Facundo Bosch and Bautista Bernasconi also come in; Bosch's last cap was in 2021. The changes follow the 42-12 defeat in Dublin, where Julián Montoya failed an HIA and Leonel Oviedo, both in doubt for Italy, were tested several times. Tobías Wade replaces Juan Cruz Mallía at fullback after a sprained knee.

lead.why: A fresh squad change ahead of Saturday's test, and the only new Argentina item in the shortlist.

teams.heading: Les Kiss signals Scotland changes; Carter Gordon, Tom Hooper in contention
teams.body: Head coach Les Kiss says he is set to change his matchday squad for the Scotland Test after the 45-22 loss to England, and the selection process is under review. Carter Gordon and Tom Hooper, recovered from injury, are candidates to return, while Rob Valetini, Ben Donaldson and Filipo Daugunu impressed off the bench at Twickenham. Kiss said: "We want competition and it hasn't been good enough, so we've got to look at that closely for sure."

lead.why: It is the only new item carrying a selection decision for the Scotland Test, where the others are post-match analysis or opinion.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy's Wales have beaten Japan twice since July 2025
teams.body: Wales have won two of the three meetings since July 2025, and the Cardiff win a year ago, sealed by Jarrod Evans' last-second penalty, gave head coach Steve Tandy his first Test victory. Wales have never lost in Cardiff against Japan, a record Saturday's 28-21 result left intact. Tandy wants Wales to 'kick on faster', pointing to four victories in 13 matches as the turnaround.

teams.heading: All Blacks cut Springboks' lead to 0.44 points after Scotland win
teams.body: The 43-21 win over Scotland at Murrayfield earned New Zealand 0.38 ranking points, lifting them to 92.65 in the World Rugby table. The Springboks' No. 1 spot is on the line when they face France in Paris on Friday, and if Les Bleus win and the All Blacks beat 10th-ranked Wales in Cardiff on Saturday, Dave Rennie's side would move to the top.

lead.why: A new item about New Zealand's own move in the World Rugby rankings, with a live route to the top if Wales fall to the All Blacks.

teams.heading: Wilco Louw starts at tighthead as Thomas du Toit drops to bench
teams.body: Erasmus has made one tweak to his starting XV for Friday's Nations Championship Test in Paris, with Stormers tighthead Wilco Louw coming in and Thomas du Toit dropping to the replacements. Planet Rugby reads the call as a set-piece decision, with Louw packing down alongside Ox Nche and Malcolm Marx. Cobus Reinach replaces Grant Williams as replacement scrum-half; the starting XV is otherwise unchanged from the 66-7 win over Italy in Turin.

lead.why: A fresh team selection with a clear headline change at tighthead, which a fan would act on before Friday.
